mission.display_title: Describe the distribution of the t-statistic for Normal samples
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to describe the distribution of the t-statistic for random samples from a Normal distribution — without claiming the F distribution (2.6.6) finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate through the t construction (unknown σ) — refuse treating Normal X̄ laws with known σ as having finished t.
mission.educational_intent: Produce the cognitive move from Normal sample with unknown σ to the t-statistic and its sampling distribution (CMP).
mission.learning_objective: Describe the distribution of the t-statistic for random samples from a normal distribution.
mission.concept_focus: Normal sample · unknown σ → t = (X̄−μ)/(S/√n) → t distribution (df) → refuse F.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you stated Normal sampling distributions for mean and variance (2.6.4). Today forms the t-statistic when σ is unknown.
mission.why_now: 2.6.5 is contiguous after Normal laws; F for variance ratios waits for day six.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for t-statistic — not F; not CI construction as primary.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.6.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) Write the t-statistic for a Normal random sample (CMP). (2) When do you use t rather than a Normal/z form? (3) What df warrant applies?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: t=(X̄−μ)/(S/√n) for Normal samples (CMP). Use t when σ is unknown and estimated by S. Degrees of freedom follow CMP (typically n−1 for one-sample).
